about.title: Brea Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Brea households buy and use thousands of consumer products daily, from kitchen appliances in homes near Birch Street to power tools and auto parts sold along Imperial Highway. When something goes wrong with a product's design, manufacturing, or missing warning label, the resulting injury can be sudden and severe. Orange County residents pursuing these claims benefit from California's strict liability framework, which generally focuses on the product's defect and the harm it caused rather than requiring proof the manufacturer was negligent. That said, product cases are technical: they often involve multiple potentially responsible parties, from the original manufacturer to a local retailer near Brea Mall, and the physical product itself becomes critical evidence. LawProactive doesn't practice law directly; we simply connect injured Brea residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney experienced in product defect matters. That attorney can evaluate what happened, help preserve the product, and explain the options available under California law, all without upfront cost to you.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — showing the product was defective and caused your injury may be enough. An independent attorney can help determine which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product in Brea can potentially be held liable. An attorney can help identify every party connected to how the defective product reached you.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central evidence in these claims, acting quickly to preserve it can matter. An independent attorney can advise on safely storing the item before it's lost, repaired, or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California often applies strict liability to defective product cases, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, rather than proving carelessness. An independent attorney can review your specific facts to confirm how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product in the same condition it was in when the injury occurred, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may serve as key evidence. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise on proper storage.

items.question: I bought the product from a store near Brea Mall — is the store responsible too?
items.answer: Retailers can sometimes share liability along with manufacturers and distributors, depending on the circumstances. This varies case by case, so it helps to have an independent attorney review where and how the product was sold before it reached you.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with an attorney.
